raw_response:
I am not doing anything fancy this year. On my 8 mu, I will still keep the same way that feels safe to me: 5 mu in wheat then maize after it, and 3 mu in cotton. Wheat and maize together give me grain and cash, and cotton can still bring money if the price is not too bad. I have seen too many years where changing too much causes trouble. I can use the well, but pumping costs money, so I will water at the important times, not too many times. Fertilizer also costs a lot, but if I use too little and the crop turns weak, that loss is worse, so I will put enough, about like the better farmers nearby do, but not the very highest amount.

For wheat, I will sow in early October like usual, using bought local seed. Before sowing I will put a base fertilizer, then give another bit when the wheat starts growing strongly in spring. If the leaves look yellow, I would rather add a little than let it stay hungry. After wheat harvest in June, I have to move fast for maize. There is no time for slow soil work, so I will clear the wheat and plant maize right away, with simple shallow tillage. Maize usually does well if it catches the summer rain, so if rain is okay I may only irrigate once or not much. Cotton I keep on the other 3 mu. Cotton needs more watching and more hand work, but I have grown it many years and know how to manage it. I will not spend too much on fancy seed or too many sprays, only when I really see worms or disease.
